stories.title: Terahertz light distinguishes two groups of particles trapped inside superconducting vortices
stories.desc: Scientists at Rutgers and in Estonia have used invisible light to look into tiny magnetic whirlpools, called vortices, inside a superconductor, revealing details that could help researchers develop better materials for carrying electricity.

stories.title: Electrical signals reveal hidden magnetic information in altermagnets for first time
stories.desc: Researchers have experimentally demonstrated, for the first time, that it is possible to obtain from an altermagnet a spin current that can transport magnetic information. stories.title: Theoretical method uses light to locate anyons, potential quantum computing building blocks
stories.desc: Theoretical physicists at Emory University have discovered a way to use light to detect the "spectral fingerprints" of anyons—exotic quasiparticles that emerge from the collective behavior of many electrons. stories.title: Unusual quantum states in six-layer graphene offer clues to superconductivity
stories.desc: Graphene, a material consisting of a sheet of carbon atoms arranged in a honeycomb pattern, has proved promising for various technological applications. Materials in which several layers of graphene are stacked together can exhibit different advantageous properties.

stories.title: Electrical guardrails for charge carriers: A new approach to harness graphene for solar cells
stories.desc: Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms in which electrons can move with high mobility, making it promising for high-speed electronic components. stories.title: Machine learning helps track semiconductor defects under more realistic temperature conditions
stories.desc: All materials contain inherent defects. These are not always harmful, since they can be used to engineer and introduce certain properties into a material. However, it is crucial to understand how they function and how they affect the material's properties.

stories.title: A blue laser for underwater communication and sensing
stories.desc: Researchers at EPFL have developed a chip-scale blue laser that combines stable light emission with rapid frequency control, opening possibilities for underwater communication, environmental sensing and quantum technologies.

stories.title: Confirming altermagnetism: A geometric twist offers experimental proof
stories.desc: For decades, physicists recognized only two types of magnetism that occur in materials without external influence: ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism.
